tools.name: whoami
tools.description:
[read-only] Returns who this connection (an OAuth sign-in or an API key) belongs to: userId, the account's current plan tier, and brandId/brandName when the connection is bound to one brand (null = account-wide). Call this first to learn what the connection can reach.
(Wraps GET /api/v2/ping.)

tools.name: list_brands
tools.description: [read-only] Lists the brands this connection can file content into and publish through. Use an `id` as `brandId` on create_content, publish, queues and analytics tools; "personal" means the account owner's personal accounts. A connection bound to one brand sees only that brand (and personal is null)

tools.name: list_youtube_playlists
tools.description:
[read-only] Playlists of the YouTube channel(s) a brand publishes to. Use a playlist id as `youtube.playlistId` on create_content or publish.
(Wraps GET /api/v2/youtube/playlists.)

tools.name: list_pinterest_boards
tools.description:
[read-only] Boards of the Pinterest account(s) a brand publishes to. Use a board id as `pinterest.boardId` on publish. A board is required; the one you pick is remembered as the brand's default for next time, and a publish that uses the default says so (defaultBoardApplied).

tools.name: upload_media
tools.description: [writes flayr data · `write` scope] Step 1 of attaching a LOCAL file (video or image) to a draft. Returns a single-use, short-lived `uploadUrl`. Step 2: POST the raw file bytes to it with the file's Content-Type, e.g. `curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: video/mp4" --data-binary @clip.mp4 "<uploadUrl>"`

tools.name: list_content
tools.description:
[read-only] Lists content items (drafts), newest first. Each carries `postState` ("posted" / "scheduled" / null) and `posts[]` (up to 5): where it went out, per platform, with status, live URL and failure reason.
(Wraps GET /api/v2/content.)

tools.name: get_content
tools.description: [read-only] One content item plus its live posting status: `postState` and `posts[]` (up to 20, newest first) with each post's status (scheduled · publishing · published · partial · failed · review_held · held), scheduledAt, and per-platform status, live URL and error. tools.name: create_content
tools.description: [writes flayr data · `write` scope] Creates a DRAFT content item. Nothing is posted. Give `text` plus optional media (`videoUrl` / `imageUrl`, or `videoStorageId` / `imageStorageId` from upload_media), target `platforms`, `brandId` (from list_brands; omitted → the brand last active in the dashboard)

tools.name: update_content
tools.description: [writes flayr data · `write` scope] Edits a draft in place; only the fields you pass change. (Wraps DELETE /api/v2/content/{id}.)

[read-only] A/B experiments. Content joins one by carrying the label `experiment:<id>` plus `<compareKey>:<variant>`.

tools.name: get_experiment

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_connected_accounts, list_content, get_content, combine_clips, publish, get_post, list_reviews, list_approvals, list_queues, query_insights, compare_labels, create_experiment, get_experiment_results, list_attribution_rules, list_share_rules, create_share_rule, list_publish_actions, list_post_comments, get_frame_settings · Private data: whoami, list_brands, upload_media, publish, delete_experiment, add_post_comments · Public sink: list_brands, list_connected_accounts, list_youtube_playlists, list_pinterest_boards, upload_media, get_content, create_content, update_content, combine_clips, publish, get_post, update_scheduled_post, cancel_scheduled_post, decide_review, list_approvals, decide_approval, create_queue, update_queue, delete_queue, add_queue_items, queue_item_action, remove_queue_item, reorder_queue_items, query_insights, compare_labels, create_experiment, create_text_template, list_attribution_rules, list_share_rules, create_share_rule, list_publish_actions, act_on_publish_action, add_post_comments, list_post_comments, create_frame, apply_frame, get_frame_settings, update_frame_settings · Destructive: delete_content, cancel_scheduled_post, decide_approval, delete_queue, remove_queue_item, delete_experiment, get_text_template, create_text_template, update_text_template, delete_text_template.
